Ceramicware Sectional Committee, CHD 9

FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 28 February 1990, after the draft finalized by the Ceramicware Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. Barium carbonate is one of the important raw materials widely used in ceramic industry in the manufacture of different types of ceramic dielectric capacitors for high frequency applications and for hard ferntes. The other important use is as an ingredient for the manufacture of ceramic glaze frits and fluxes; optical and ophthalmic glasses; and special cut-glasses. It is also used as an ingredient for manufacturing other electro-ceramic materials used as resistors, circuit breakers, etc. There have been a persistent demand from the Ceramic and Glass Industry for bringing out an Indian Standard to enable them to keep pace with the developing technology. The publication of this standard meets their long pending demand. This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards on barium carbonate. Other standards in the series are: IS 1151 : 1984 Specification for barium carbonate, pesticidal grade IS 3205 : 1984 Specification for precipitated barium carbonate, technical For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for precipitated barium carbonate for ceramic and glass industry. 2 REFERENCES 2.1 The Indian Standards listed below are necessary adjuncts to this standard IS No. IS 1070 : 1977 IS 2263 : 1979 Title Specification for water for general laboratory use ( second revision ) Methods of preparation of indicator solutions for volumetric analysis ( first revision ) Methods of preparation of standard solutions for colonmetric and volumetric analysis ( first revision ) Glossary of terms relating to ceramicware ( first revision ) Methods for random sampling IS No. IS 12305 : 1988 Title Laboratory sintered ( fritted ) filters, porosity grading, classification and designation

3 TERMINOLOGY 3.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS 2731 : 1975 shall apply. 4 GRADES 4.1 There shall be two grades of materials, namely: Grade 1 For use in dieletric ceramics, hard ferrites an d electro-ceramic materials; and Grade 2 For use in ceramic glaze, frits, colours and glasses. 5 REQUIREMENTS 5.1 The material shall be in the form of fine white powder and shall be free flowing. 5.2 The material shall comply with the requirements prescribed in Table 1 when tested according to methods given in Annex A. Reference to the relevant clauses of Annex A is given in col 5 of Table 1.

IS 12928 : 1990 6 PACKING AND MARKING 6.1 Packing The material shall be packed in jute bags lined with polyethylene films or HDPE bags. The bags shall be securely closed. 6.2 Marking The bags shall bear legibly and indelibly the following information: a) Name and grade of the material, b) Indication of the source of manufacture, c) Net mass, d) Date of manufacture, e) Batch number, and f) Word 'POISON' ( in red ink ). 6.2.1 The packages may also be marked with the Standard Mark, details for which may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 7 SAMPLING 7.1 The method of drawing representative samples of the material and the criteria for conformity shall be as prescribed in Annex B.

ANNEX A

( Clause 5.2 and Table 1 )
METHODS OF TEST FOR BARIUM CARBONATE FOR CERAMIC AND GLASS INDUSTRY A-1 QUALITY OF REAGENTS A-1.1 Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and distilled water ( see IS 1070 : 1977 ) shall be used in tests. NOTE -- 'Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities which affect the results of analysis A-2 DETERMINATION OF BARIUM A-2.0 Outline of the Method Two methods are prescribed for determination of barium, namely, volumetric method and gravimetric method. In volumetric method, barium is precipitated as barium chromate which is then dissolved in dilute hydrochloric acid and treated with solid potassium iodide. The liberated iodine is titrated against standard sodium thiosulphate solution. In gravimetric method, barium is estimated as barium sulphate after dissolving in hydrochloric acid and precipitating with sulphuric acid In case of dispute, volumetric method shall be followed. A-2.1 Volumetric Method A-2.1.1 Reagents A-2.1.1.1 Dilute hydrochloric acid -- 1 : 1 ( v/v ). A-2.1.1.2 Concentrated hydrochloric acid A-2.1.1.3 Concentrated ammonium hydroxide -- 20 percent ( m/m ). A-2.1.1.4 Ammonium chloride -- solid A-2.1.1.5 Hydrogen sulphide -- gas. A-2.1.1.6 Lead acetate paper A-2.1.1.7 Methyl orange indicator -- Dissolve 0.1 g of methyl orange in 100 ml of water. A-2.1.1.8 Glacial acetic acid A-2.1.1.9 Ammonium acetate solution -- 30 percent ( m, v ). 2 A 2.1.1.10 Ammonium chromate solution -- 10 percent ( m/v ), neutral to methyl orange. A-2.1.1.11 Ammonium chromate solution -- one percent ( m/v ), neutral to methyl orange. A-2.1.1.12 Ammonium carbonate solution -- approximately 20 percent ( m/v ) A-2.1.1.13 Silver nitrate solution -- approximately 2 percent ( m/v ) A-2.1.1.14 Dilute nitric acid, approximately 2 N. A-2.1.1.15 Potassium iodide -- solid. A-2.1.1.16 Standard sodium thiosulphate solution -- 0.1 N. A-2.1.1.17 Starch indicator solution -- one percent. A-2.1.2 Procedure Weigh accurately about 0 25 g of the material and dissolve in about 30 ml of dilute hydrochloric acid Add 100 ml of water, boil and filter. Wash the residue with water. Collect the filtrate and the washings in a 500-ml beaker and make alkaline with ammonium hydroxide. Add about one gram of ammonium chloride, pass hydrogen sulphide gas and the filter. Again pass hydrogen sulphide gas in filtrate till no turbidity appears. Boil the filtrate to completely drive away hydrogen sulphide gas and test by lead acetate paper. Acidify the solution with dilute hydrochloric acid using methyl orange indicator. Add 5 to 6 drops of mixture containing glacial acetic and ammonia acetate solution ( 30 percent ) in 1 : 1 ratio or 5 to 6 drops of diluted liquid ammonia to neutralize any free mineral acid. Heat the solution and add an excess of ammonium chromate solution. A-2.1.2.1 Allow the precipitate of barium chromate to settle for an hour. Filter through a filter paper ( No. 42 ) and wash with one percent ammonium chromate solution until the filtrate is free of soluble strontium and calcium salts which

IS 12928 : 1990 are tested if a portion of the filtrate produces no cloudiness with ammonium hydroxide and ammonium carbonate. Finally wash the residue free of ammonium chromate with water till a portion of the filtrate gives only slight reddish brown colour with silver nitrate solution. A-2.1.2.2 Pierce the filter paper containing the barium chromate precipitate and wash the precipitate into a beaker with hot dilute nitric acid Dilute the solution to about 200 ml and boil Add ammonium acetate solution to neutralize any free nitric acid. Heat and add sufficient ammonium chromate solution. Filter and repeat washings as in A-2 1.2.1 above Dissolve the precipitate of barium chromate finally in 50 to 100 ml of dilute hydrochloric acid, add about 2 g of solid potassium iodide and allow to react for ten minutes. Titrate the liberated iodine with standard sodium thiosulphate using starch as indicator. A-2 1.3 Calculation Barium, percent by mass = where V = volume in ml of standard sodium throsulphate required for the titration, and M = mass in g of the material taken for the test. A-2.2 Gravimetric Method A-2.2.1 Reagents A-2.2.1.1 Dilute hydrochloric acid -- 5 N A-2.2.1.2 Sulphuric acid A-2.2 1.3 Dilute sulphuric acid -- 1:2 A-2.2.2 Procedure Weigh accurately about 1 g of the sample and dissolve in 20 ml of water Add 1 ml of dilute hydrochloric acid ( 5 N ). Heat the solution to boiling, add 5 ml of hot dilute sulphuric acid (1 2) slowly with constant stirring Cool, dilute to about 100 ml and allow to stand for 4 hours at 60�C. Filter the precipitate through filter paper ( Whatman No. 42 or equivalent ) Wash the precipitate twice with dilute sulphuric acid ( 1 : 99 ) and then with hot water till it is free from chloride and sulphate. Dry the precipitate and then ignite slowly at a low flame and finally at 800�C in a furnace till constant mass is obtained. A-2.2.3 Calculation Barium ( as Ba ), percent by mass = where M1 = mass in g of the ignited residue, and M = mass in g of the material taken for the test. A-3 DETERMINATION OF VOLATILE MATTER A-3.1 Procedure Weigh accurately about 5 g of the material in a clean squat type glass weighing bottle, previously dried and weighed. Place the weighing bottle in an oven maintained at 105 � 2�C till constant mass is obtained. A-3.2 Calculation Moisture, percent by mass = 100 where M1 = mass in g of the weighing bottle with the sample before drying, M2 = mass in g of the weighing bottle with the sample after drying, and M = mass in g of the empty weighing bottle A-4 DETERMINATION OF MATTER INSOLUBLE IN HYDROCHLORIC ACID A-4.1 Reagent A-4.1.1 Concentrated Hydrochloric Acid A-4.2 Procedure Mix 10 g of the material with 100 ml of water and add slowly 10 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid Dilute with water to 200 ml and heat on the steam-bath for 30 minutes Filter the hot solution through a previous dried and weighed sintered glass crucible No. P-16 ( see IS 12305: 1988 ). Wash the residue with water slightly acidified with hydrochloric acid. Again wash the crucible with hot water till the filtrate is free from acid. Place the crucible in an oven maintained at 105�C � 2�C till constant weight. Cool the crucible in a desiccator and weigh. A-4.3 Calculation Matter insoluble in hydrochloric acid, percent by mass = where M2 = miss in g of the crucible after filtration, M1 = mass in g of the crucible before filtration, and M = mass in g of the material taken for the test. A-5 TEST FOR FREE ALKALI A-5.0 Outline of the Method Free alkali is determined by titration with standard hydrochloric acid. A-5.1 Reagents A-5.1.1 Standard Hydrochloric Acid -- 0 02 N. A-5.1.2 Phenolphthalein Indicator Dissolve 0 1 g of phenolphthalein in 100 ml of 60 percent rectified spirit.

3

IS 12928 : 1990 A-5.2 Procedure Shake 2 0 g of the material for 5 minutes with 30 ml of carbon dioxide free water. Filter and add 5 drops of phenolphthalein to 20 ml of the filtrate. Titrate this solution with standard hydrochloric acid. A-5.2.1 The material shall be taken to have passed the test, if not more than 2.5 ml of standard hydrochloric acid is required for the titration. A-7.1.2 Concentrated Hydrochloric Acid A-7.1.3 Bromine ( Saturated ) A-7.1.4 Sodium Carbonate A-7.1.5 Potassium Nitrate A-7.1.6 Methyl Orange -- Dissolve 0.1 g of methyl orange in 60 ml of rectified spirit and dilute with water to 100 ml. A-7.1.7 Barium Chloride Solution -- 5 percent. A-7.1.8 Dilute Hydrochloric Acid -- approximate 0 1 N. A-7.1.9 Concentrated Hydrofluoric Acid A-7.1.10 Concentrated Sulphuric Acid A-7.2 Procedure Weigh exactly 5 g of the sample and transfer the sample to a 400-ml beaker. Make it to a paste with water. Then add 15 ml concentrated nitric acid, 5 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid and 0.5 ml of bromine. Boil and allow to stand the covered beaker on steam bath for 30 minutes. Evaporate to dryness Add 10 drops of concentrated hydrochloric acid and dilute it to 200 ml with water Heat to the boiling point. Allow the covered beaker to stand overnight. Filter through a close filter paper ( Whatman No 42 ). Wash with hot water. Discard the filtrate. Ash the precipitate in the paper in a platinum crucible. Fuse the mixture with 3 g of sodium carbonate and 0.5 g of potassium nitrate. A-7.2.1 Leach the melted mass with water. Transfer the contents of the crucible to 250-ml volumetric flask. Fill up to the mark with water and mix. Filter through dry paper ( discarding the first 10 ml ) into a dry volumetric flask of 200-ml up to the mark. Transfer the contents of the 200-ml volumetric flask quantitatively to a 600 ml beaker. Add few drops of methyl orange. Acidify with 6 N hydrochloric acid. Boil to remove carbon dioxide. Neutralize and then acidify with 0 1 N hydrochloric acid Heat to boil and add while stirring 5 ml of 5 percent barium chloride solution. Allow overnight for setting Filter the precipitate through Whatman No. 42 filter paper and wash with a little hot water till free from chloride. Dry and ignite the paper in platinum crucible A-7.2.2 To the ash add 1 ml of 40 percent hydrofluoric acid, and one drop of concentrated sulphuric acid. Again ignite and weigh. A-7.3 Calculation Total sulphur ( as SO4 ), percent by mass = where M1 = mass in g of the precipitate, and M2 = mass in g of the material ( A-7.3 ) taken for the test. 4

A-6 DETERMINATION OF WATER SOLUBLE SULPHIDES
A-6.0 Outline of the Method Water soluble sulphides are determined iodimetrically A-6.1 Reagents A-6.1.1 Standard Iodine Solution -- approximately 0 01 N ( see IS 2316 : 1968 ). A-6.1.2 Concentrated Hydrochloric Acid A-6.1.3 Standard Sodium Thiosulphate Solution-- 0.01 N ( see IS 2316 : 1968 ) A-6.1.4 Starch Indicator Solution -- One percent contains 0 01 g of mercuric iodide ( see IS 2263 : 1979 ). A 6.2 Procedure Weigh accurately about 5 g of the material, add 100 ml of water; warm slightly and filter. Wash the residue with hot water and cool the filtrate. Transfer the filtrate to a conical flask containing a measured quantity of 50 ml of standard iodine solution. Add 10 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid and titrate the excess of iodine with standard sodium thiosulphate solution using starch indicator. Carry out the blank determination simultaneously under similar conditions. A-6.3 Calculation Water soluble sulphides ( as S ), percent by mass = where N = normality of the standard sodium thiosulphate solution, V1 = volume in ml of standard sodium thiosulphate solution used in the blank titration, V2 = volume in ml of standard sodium thiosulphate solution used in the titration, and M1 = mass in g of the material taken for the test. A-7 ESTIMATION OF TOTAL SULPHUR A-7.1 Reagents A-7.1.1 Concentrated Nitric Acid

IS 12928 : 1990 A-8 DETERMINATION OF ALKALI AND OTHER METAL SULPHATES A-8.0 Outline of the Method Alkali and other metals are determined gravimetrically as sulphates. A-8.1 Reagents A-8.1.1 Dilute mately 5 N. Hydrochloric Acid -- approximeter when distilled water is atomized. Adjust the spot to 100 or 200 as required by atomizing highest concentration ( 10 ppm solution ). Take the reading in quick succession of the other calibrating solution. Atomize distilled water in between the readings. It is better to repeat the series of readings to feel safe about it. A-9.3.3 After all the readings are over, plot the graph of concentration on X axis, and galvanometer reading on Y axis. This curve is used for determining the sodium concentration of unknown solution. A-9.4 Procedure A-9.4.1 Take 5 g of material powder in a 100-ml beaker. Make it to a paste with water. Add drop by drop concentrated hydrochloric acid to dissolve. When all the carbonate is dissolved, just neutralize the solution to pH 7 with ammonia solution. Keep the solution on a water bath so that excess ammonia expels out Now filter the solution through Whatman 42 filter paper into a 250-ml volumetric flask, wash well and make up the solution to 250-ml mark. Atomize this solution in the flame photometer adjusting the sodium filter and note the galvanometer reading for the unknown solution. A-9.4.2 From the curve, find out the concentration of sodium for the corresponding galvanometer reading. A-9.5 Calculation Sodium ( as Na ), ppm = Sodium oxide ( as Na2O ), ppm = Na � 1.35 A-10 DETERMINATION OF TOTAL IRON A-10.0 Outline of the Method Total iron is determined colorimetrically by visual comparison. A-10.1 Apparatus A-10.1.1 Nessler Cylinders � 100-ml capacity. A-10.2 Reagents A-10.2.1 Concentrated Hydrochloric Acid A-10.2.2 Ammonium Persulphate -- solid A-10.2.3 Butanolic Potassium Thiocyanate Solution Dissolve 10 g of potassium thiocyanate in 10 ml of water. Add sufficient n-butanol to make up to 100 ml, shake vigorously until the solution is clear. A-10.2.4 Standard Iron Solution Dissolve 0.702 g of ferrous ammonium sulphate [ FeSO 4 ( NH 4 )2SO4 ( 6H2O )] in water, add 10 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid and dilute to one litre. One millilitre of this solution is equivalent to 0.1 mg of iron ( as Fe ). 5

A-8.1.2 Dilute Sulphuric 5 N A-8.2 Procedure

Acid -- approximately

Dissolve 5 g of the material in 100 ml water and 20 ml dilute hydrochloric acid. Heat to boiling, add 12 ml to 15 ml of dilute sulphuric acid and allow to stand for two hours Filter, evaporate the filtrate to dryness, ignite gently and weigh the residue. A-8.3 Calculation Alkali and other metals ( as SO4 ), percent by mass = where M1 = mass in. g of the residue, and M = mass in g of the material taken for the test. A-9 ESTIMATION OF SODIUM OXIDE BY FLAME PHOTOMETER A-9.1 Reagents A-9.1.1 Sodium Chloride -- AR grade. A-9.1.2 Stock Solution of Sodium Chloride Dissolve 2.545 g of AR grade sodium chloride in distilled water in 1 000-ml volumetric flask and dilute to the mark. Shake well taking care that the solution does not leak or come in contact with fingers. This solution contains 1 mg of sodium ( Na ) per ml of the solution. A-9.2 Instrument Used A-9.2.1 Flame Photometer -- with a filter for sodium. A-9.3 Preparation of Calibration Curve A-9.3.1 To prepare calibrating solution containing 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 ppm of sodium, transfer 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 ml each of stock solution in 5 different one litre volumetric flasks by means of pipette and dilute up to the mark with distilled water. Pour the calibrating solution into 1 000 ml or 500-ml plastic bottles and label them as 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 ppm of sodium, respectively. A-9.3.2 Bring the sodium filter in flame photometer in position. The galvanometer spot is adjusted to left hand zero of the scale of galvano-

IS 12928 : 1990 A-10.3 Procedure Weigh accurately about 0.25 g of the material and dissolve in 10 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid. Dilute with 10 ml of water, add 30 mg of ammonium persulphate, warm and filter into a Nessler cylinder. Cool and add 5 ml of butanolic potassium thiocyanate solution. Add 5 ml of butanolic potassium thiocyanate to another Nessler cylinder containing 10 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid, 30 mg of ammonium persulphate and 10 ml of water. Add slowly standard iron solution into the second Nessler cylinder from a burette until after thorough mixing the colours in the two Nessler cylinders match. A-10.4 Calculation Iron ( as Fe 2 O 3 ), percent by mass = where V = volume in ml of standard iron solution required, and M = mass in g of the material taken for the test. A-11 TAP DENSITY A-11.1 Apparatus A-11.1.1 Measuring Cylinder -- 100-ml capacity. A-11.1.2 Rubber Base Pod A-11.1.3 Funnel A-11.2 Procedure Take sufficient quantity of the dried sample and slip it gently and smoothly through the funnel into the measuring cylinder of 100-ml capacity, up to the 100-ml mark without knocking. Stopper with rubber cork and give constant tapping from a height of 15 cm on the rubber base pad for 25 times. Note the volume and mass of the material A-11.3 Calculation Tap density, g/ml = where M = mass in g of the material, and V = volume in ml of the material, A-12 RESIDUE ON SIEVE A-12.1 Apparatus A-12.1.1 Sieve -- IS sieve, 63 micron. A-12.2 Reagents A-12.2.1 Refined Linseed Oil A-12.2.2 Petroleum Hydrocarbon Solvent -- 145/ 205. A-12.3 Procedure Weigh accurately the appropriate quantity of the sample dried at 100 � 2�C for 2 hours. Transfer 10 g of sample to a glazed porcelain plate. Thoroughly incorporate sufficient quantity of refined linseed oil with a pallete knife without any grinding action until a uniform paste is obtained Mix the paste with 100 ml of petroleum hydrocarbon solvent 145/205 and transfer the mixture on to a 63 micron IS sieve by rinsing with further quantities of petroleum hydrocarbon solvent Wash the residue left on the sieve with petroleum hydrocarbon solvent gently brushing with a soft camel hair brush until the washings are clear. Dry the residue to a constant mass at 105 � 2�C. A-12.3.1 Calculation Residue on sieve = M � 10 where M = mass in g of the residue left on the sieve.

ANNEX B ( Clause 7.1 ) SAMPLING OF PRECIPITATED BARIUM CARBONATE FOR CERAMIC AND GLASS INDUSTRY B-1 SCALE OF SAMPLING B-1.1 Lot All the packages in a single consignment of the material and from a single batch of manufacture shall constitute a lot. If a consignment is declared or known to consist of packages from different batches of manufacture, the batches shall be marked separately and the packages in each such batch shall constitute separate lots. B-1.2 The number of packages to be selected from the lot shall depend upon the size of the lot and shall be in accordance with Table 2. 6 Table 2 Number of Packages to be Selected ( Clause B-1 2 )
Number of Packages to be Selected n (2) 5 6 7 8 9 10

Lot Size N (1) U p to 1 00 101 to 300 301 to 500 501 to 800 801 to 1 300 1 301 and above

B-1.3 These packages shall be selected at random from the lots and in order to ensure the

IS 12928 : 1990 randomness of selecticn, random number table may be used as described in IS 4905 : 1968. B-2 TEST SAMPLES AND REFEREE SAMPLES B-2.1 Draw with an appropriate sampling instrument small portions of the material from different parts of the packages in the sample. The total quantity of material so drawn from each package shall be approximately three times the quantity required for carrying out the tests for all the requirements. B-2.2 Mix thoroughly the portions drawn from the same package to form an individual sample representative of the package. Also mix together equal portions from the individual samples to form a composite sample representative of the whole lot. B-2.3 Divide the individual samples and the composite sample into three sets of test samples, each set shall have individual samples representing each package and a composite sample. Transfer these test samples immediately to thoroughly dried sample containers which shall then be sealed air-tight and labelled with all the particulars of sampling given under B-1 . One of these sets shall be for the purchaser, another for the supplier and the third for the referee. Referee samples shall consist of a set of individual samples and a composite sample marked for the purpose. Referee samples shall bear the seals of the purchaser and the manufacturer, and shall be kept at a place agreed to between the two. It shall be used in case of dispute between the two. B-3 NUMBER OF TESTS B-3.1 Tests for the material insoluble in hydrochloric acid, water soluble sulphides and barium content shall be conducted on each of the individual samples in the set of test samples. B-3.2 Tests for the remaining characteristics shall be conducted on the composite samples. B-4 CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY B-4 1 A lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements of this specification, if the requirements given in B-4.2 and B-4.3 are satisfied B-4.2 The individual samples, when tested for material insoluble in hydrochloric acid, water soluble sulphides and barium content shall all satisfy the requirements of the specification individually. B-4.3 For the remaining characteristics which have been tested on the composite sample, all the test results shall satisfy the corresponding requirements of the specification.

The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
